NAHHAS:v3p283/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p283/r1.claim: For ماذا خلق, ما may be the subject and ذا a relative predicate, with an omitted object of خلق; alternatively ما is its object and ذا is extra.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r1.anchor: ما في موضع رفع بالابتداء وخبره ذا وذا بمعنى الذي وخلق واقع على هاء محذوفة

NAHHAS:v3p283/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p283/r2.claim: الظالمون is a subject and في ضلال مبين its predicate.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r2.anchor: بل الظالمون ) رفع بالابتداء ( في ضلال مبين ) في موضع الخبر

TABRISI:31:11-14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:11-14/r10.claim: In fa-arūnī mādhā khalaqa, mādhā functions as one accusative noun meaning what thing, the object of khalaqa, and the clause is governed by arūnī.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r10.anchor: تقديره أي شيء خلق فماذا بمنزلة اسم واحد في موضع نصب بأنه مفعول خلق

TABRISI:31:14-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14-15/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14-15/r2.claim: The created heavens and earth prove God's creation; idols created nothing, and worshippers cannot answer this, showing their manifest departure from truth.
TABRISI:31:14-15/r2.anchor: أي هذا الذي ذكرت من السموات على عظمها وكبر حجمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r9.claim: “This is God’s creation” points to the created things listed and challenges the unbelievers with the evidence they display.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r9.anchor: هذا خلق الله إشارة إلى ما ذكر من مخلوقاته، وبخ بذلك الكفار وأظهر حجته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r10.claim: Here “creation” means the created object, as in the expression “a dirham minted by the prince.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r10.anchor: والخلق بمعنى المخلوق، كقولهم: درهم ضرب الأمير، أي مضروبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r1.claim: The challenge asks what the idols created after God’s creatures have been listed; “what” can be a relative object or an interrogative joined to a relative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r1.anchor: ويجوز في ماذا أن تكون كلها موصولة بمعنى الذي، وتكون مفعولا ثانيا لأروني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r2.claim: Sibawayh records the uncommon use of the whole expression “mādhā” as a single relative pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r2.anchor: واستعمال ماذا كلها موصولا قليل، وقد ذكره سيبويه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r3.claim: The passage shifts from reproaching the idolaters to judging them manifestly confused, since they abandon their creator for an idol.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p411/r3.anchor: ثم أضرب عن توبيخهم وتبكيتهم إلى التسجيل عليهم بأنهم في حيرة واضحة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.claim: The account specially warns fathers who pressure sons to abandon Islam, echoing the warning in 29:8: Luqmān lovingly urged his son toward the same principles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.anchor: There is a special warning in this for people who in those times were oppressing their sons to leave Islam

RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r1.claim: God alone creates; since everything besides Him is created, people should worship the Creator rather than created things.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r1.anchor: يعني الله خالق وغيره ليس بخالق فكيف تتركون عبادة الخالق

RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r2.claim: Mubin can mean manifest or clear to a rational person as being misguidance.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r2.anchor: أي بين أو مبين للعاقل أنه ضلال

RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r3.claim: Turning slightly right or left is a lesser deviation than turning backward; the one who seeks God while distracted by worldly things may arrive only after hardship, while a direct seeker arrives quickly and easily.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r3.anchor: فمن يطلبه ويلتفت إلى غيره من الدنيا وغيرها فهو ضال

RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r4.claim: One who turns away from God never reaches the destination, even after traveling for a long time.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r4.anchor: وأما الذي تولى لا يصل إلى المقصود أصلا

RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r5.claim: The wrongdoers are idolaters who place worship incorrectly or place themselves in the worship of something other than God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126#3/r5.anchor: والمراد بالظالمين المشركون الواضعون لعبادتهم في غير موضعها

STUDYQURAN:31:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:11/r1.claim: The verse challenges idolaters to substantiate their claim that idols participate in creation; it invokes questions showing that no one created the heavens or earth besides God.
STUDYQURAN:31:11/r1.anchor: challenges the idolaters to substantiate their claim that their idols have some part in the creative process

STUDYQURAN:31:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:11/r2.claim: For the phrase manifest error, the commentary directs readers to its discussion at 36:24.

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r1.claim: This points to the heavens, earth, mountains, animals, and plants just described.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r1.anchor: {هاذا} الذي ذكر من السموات والأرض والجبال والحيوان والنبات

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r2.claim: Khalq means the created thing: a verbal noun stands for its passive object by extension.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r2.anchor: مخلوقة كضرب الأمير أي : مضروبه فأقيم المصدر مقام المفعول توسعا

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r3.claim: The challenge is to idolaters: show what the beings made God's partners in worship have created and why they deserve worship with Him.

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r4.claim: Mādhā may be one interrogative meaning what thing, governed by khalaqa; alternatively mā is subject and dhā with its relative clause is predicate, and arūnī suspends the question syntactically.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r4.anchor: وماذا بمنزلة اسم واحد بمعنى أي : شيء نصب بخلق أو ما مرتفع بالابتداء وخبره ذا وصلته

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r5.claim: After rebuking Quraysh, the shift declares their plain misguidance; calling them wrongdoers marks their injustice as associating partners with God.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r5.anchor: {بل الظالمون فى ضلال مبين} إضراب عن تبكيتهم أي : كفار قريش

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r6.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r6.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān applies Quraysh's manifest error to other peoples who acted like them.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r6.anchor: في "فتح الرحمن" بل هذا الذي قريش فيه ضلال مبين فذكرهم بالصفة

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r7.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the polytheists err by making the powerless creature share worship with the All-Powerful Creator.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (بلكه مشركان در كمراهى آشكارانند كه عاجزرا باقادر

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r8.claim: Tawḥīd is the highest virtue and shirk the greatest sin: tawḥīd's light burns monotheists' sins, while shirk's fire consumes polytheists' good deeds.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r8.anchor: واعلم أن التوحيد أفضل الفضائل كما أن الشرك أكبر الكبائر وللتوحيد نور كما أن للشرك نارا

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r9.claim: Tawḥīd and remembrance are not limited to set times, unlike fasting and prayers, because they are the best worship and nearest approach.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r9.anchor: ولكون التوحيد أفضل العبادات وذكر الله أقرب القربات لم يقيد بالزمان والأوقات بخلاف سائر الأعمال

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r10.claim: Escape from error comes through guidance to tawḥīd and sincere worship of God.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r10.anchor: فالخلاص من الضلالة إنما هو بالهداية إلى التوحيد وإخلاص العبادةالحميد

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r11.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r11.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever affirms God's oneness and rejects what is worshipped besides Him protects life and property; God judges hidden sincerity in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r11.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من قال لا إله إلا الله وكفر بما يعبد من دون الله

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r12.claim: Manifest and hidden shirk, and deeds founded on them, are rejected; sincere knowledge and deeds are beloved and draw near to God.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r12.anchor: ثم علم المشرك بالشرك الجلي وكذا عمله وإن كانا في صورة الحسنة كلاهما مردود

BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r13.claim: Ostentation and seeking reputation move between heaven and earth, then are struck back against their owner's face.
BURSEVI:v7p53#3/r13.anchor: فإن عمل الرياء والسمعة يدور بين السماء والأرض ثم يضرب به على وجه صاحبه

TAB-FULL:v18p545/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p545/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p545/r1.claim: The listed creation belongs to God alone, whose divinity and worship are exclusive; the challenge asks polytheists to show what their idols created to deserve worship.
TAB-FULL:v18p545/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {هذا خلق الله} [لقمان: 11] ما ذكر من خلق السماوات والأرض، وما بث من الدواب

TAB-FULL:v18p545/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p545/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p545/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the listed creation as the heavens, earth, animals, and plants, and says the challenged rivals are the idols people invoke.
TAB-FULL:v18p545/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {هذا خلق الله} [لقمان: 11] ما ذكر من خلق السماوات والأرض، وما بث من الدواب

TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r1.claim: The polytheists worship idols because they have strayed from truth and uprightness, not because the idols create anything.
TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r1.anchor: تأمله، ونظر فيه، وفكر بعقل أنه ضلال لا هدى

TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r2.claim: The deviation is manifest to anyone who reflects, considers it, and thinks rationally: it is error, not guidance.
TAB-FULL:v18p545#2/r2.anchor: فكر بعقل أنه ضلال لا هدى

TABATABAI:31:11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:11/r2.claim: After showing God's creation and governance of the heavens, earth, and their contents, the verse challenges polytheists to show any creation by their alleged gods.
TABATABAI:31:11/r2.anchor: لما رأهم خلقه وتدبيره تعالى للسماوات والأرض وما عليها فأثبت به ربوبيته وألوهيته

TABATABAI:31:11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:11/r3.claim: The challenge establishes God's sole divinity and lordship: if the idols cannot create anything, they cannot be gods or lords.
TABATABAI:31:11/r3.anchor: فإن لم يقدروا على إرادة شيء ثبت بذلك وحدانيته تعالى في الوهيته وربوبيته

TABATABAI:31:11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:11/r4.claim: Though polytheists assign governance, not creation, to idols, creation and governance are inseparable; a real governor would create what it governs.
TABATABAI:31:11/r4.anchor: لأنه نسب إلى الله خلقا هو بعينه تدبير من غير انفكاك

TABATABAI:31:11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:11/r5.claim: The imperative challenge is spoken by the Prophet, since this form of address cannot properly come from anyone else.
TABATABAI:31:11/r5.anchor: وقد سيقت الآية خطابا من النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لأن نوع هذا الخطاب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r4.claim: The challenge to show what others created is directed at the polytheists and their idols.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r4.anchor: ثم قال: {هذا خلق الله فأروني} [لقمان: 11] ، يعني: المشركين. {ماذا خلق الذين من دونه} [لقمان: 11] ، يعني: الأوثان التي يعبدونها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r5.claim: The idols created nothing and offer no proof; the wrongdoers are polytheists in manifest error.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r5.anchor: فلم تكن لهم حجة فقال: {بل الظالمون} [لقمان: 11] المشركين. {في ضلال مبين} بين.

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r3.claim: The listed cosmic and earthly phenomena are God's creation, and the challenge asks what anything worshipped besides Him has created.

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r4.claim: The wrongdoers are the polytheists, who wrong the meaning of creation and divinity and depart from manifest truth.
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r4.anchor: pek büyük zâlim olan, şirki irtikâb eyleyen müşrikler

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r5.claim: They falsely attribute divine creative power to creatures.
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r5.anchor: Bir taraftan mahlûka hâlık kudreti isnad ederek “filan şunu yarattı, falan şunu yarattı” diye yalan söylerler

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r6.claim: They also worship objects known to have created nothing.
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r6.anchor: bir taraftan da hiçbir şey yaratmadığı

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r7.claim: In response to the question whether human crafts and inventions count as creation, Elmalılı says wisdom is God's gift, so He is their creator too and deserves thanks; to the wise, shirk is grave injustice.
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r7.anchor: hikmetin Allah vergisi olduğu ve binâen‘aleyh hikmet ile yapılan şeylerin de hâlıkı Allah olduğu bilinerek O’na şükredilmesi lâzım geleceği

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r9.claim: The created heavens and earth display God’s majesty and expose the inability of those worshipped besides Him to create anything.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r9.anchor: هذا خلق الله العزيز في كبريائه ، فأروني ماذا خلق الذين عبدتم من دونه في أرضه وسمائه

ITQAN:v4p328/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p328/r6.speaker: البارزي
ITQAN:v4p328/r6.claim: Al-Barizi illustrates preference for lighter diction with آمن over صدق, آثرك الله over فضلك, أتى over أعطى, أنذر over خوف, خير لكم over أفضل لكم, and shorter nominal forms and تنكح.
ITQAN:v4p328/r6.anchor: و ﴿ آثرك ﴾ ﴿ الله ﴾ أخف من ( فضلك ) و ﴿ أتى ﴾ أخف من ( أعطى )

ITQAN:v2p557/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p557/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p557/r10.claim: A demonstrative distinguishes its referent as fully as possible by making it present to the hearer’s senses.
ITQAN:v2p557/r10.anchor: وبالإشارة لتمييزه أكمل تمييز بإحضاره في ذهن السامع حسا نحو ﴿ هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه ﴾

SAMIN-DURR:31:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:11/r1.claim: ما in ماذا خلق is interrogative; al-Samin refers to his fuller treatment in al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:31:11/r1.anchor: قوله: { ماذا خلق }: " ما " استفهام. وقد تقدم تحقيق هذا في البقرة.

ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n11/r1.claim: Here 'the evildoers' are those who attribute divine powers to beings or things other than God.
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n11/r1.anchor: Sc., "who ascribe divine powers to beings or things other than God".

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r1.claim: The addressees acknowledge that God created all the things cited above; they are challenged to name anything their other deities created that would justify sharing God’s rights.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r1.anchor: all the above pointed things have been made by God and the addressees of this verse also admit this fact.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r2.claim: Calling the wrongdoers manifestly astray indirectly expresses pity: they have no grounds for treating other deities as God’s partners.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r2.anchor: express pity on such people by addressing them in an indirect way: these people who have transgressed against their souls do not have any reason

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p118/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p118/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p118/r1.claim: The introduction ends at verse 11; Luqmān’s intervening counsel reinforces gratitude to God alone, and verse 20 resumes the argument from signs around people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p118/r1.anchor: The introductory part of this sūrah ended on verse 11 on the words

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r1.claim: This refers to the heavens, earth, and other enumerated matters; خلق الله means God's created work.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r1.anchor: أي ما ذكر من السموات والأرض وسائر الأمور المعدودة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r2.claim: أروني means inform or show me; an implied condition is 'once you know this,' and the challenge asks what alleged partners created to merit worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r2.anchor: أي أعلموني وأخبروني والفاء واقعة في جواب شرط مقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r3.claim: One parsing treats ماذا as a single interrogative pronoun, fronted as the object of خلق.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون أسما واحدا إستفهاميا ويكون مفعولا لخلق مقدما

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r4.claim: Another parsing makes ما an interrogative subject and ذا a relative predicate; the clause fills أروني's second object slot, with the relative pronoun omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r4.anchor: ( ما ) وحدها أسم إستفهام مبتدأ و ( ذا )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan notes a rarer parsing of ماذا as a single relative pronoun functioning as أروني's second object, with its antecedent omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r5.anchor: فقد أستعمل كذلك على قلة على ما قال أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r6.claim: The turn from demanding proof to declaring manifest error ends direct argument because they cannot understand its premises or be moved by refutation.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r6.anchor: إضراب عن تبكيتهم بما ذكر إلى التسجيل عليهم بالضلال البين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r7.claim: Calling them wrongdoers instead of using a pronoun shows shirk as putting things wrongly and exceeding bounds, wronging themselves through eternal punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82#2/r7.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع ضميرهم للدلالة على أنهم بإشراكهم واضعون للشيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p286/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p286/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p286/r1.claim: “This” points to what has just been described and can be seen; the false gods created none of it, and the idolaters are plainly astray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p286/r1.anchor: {هذا} يعني الذي ذكرت مما تعاينون، {خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه}

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r7.claim: The things just described are God's creation; the challenge asks what the alleged gods created to deserve sharing in His divinity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r7.anchor: هذا الذي ذكر مخلوقه فماذا خلق

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r8.claim: Bayḍāwī parses mādhā either as the object of khalaqa, or as mā in the subject position with dhā and its relative clause as predicate; fa-arūnī is suspended by the question.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r8.anchor: ماذا } نصب ب { خلق } أو ما مرتفع بالابتداء

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r9.claim: The verse turns from rebuking the idolaters to declaring their unmistakable error; naming them as wrongdoers in place of a pronoun signals that shirk is injustice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r9.anchor: إضراب عن تبكيتهم إلى التسجيل عليهم بالضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r1.claim: God's ordered creation establishes His might and wisdom, and therefore His sole divinity and the obligation to worship Him alone, just as He alone creates.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r1.anchor: وجوب توحيده في العبادة كما توحد بالخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r2.claim: Everything people observe is God's creation; He possesses unmatched majesty and has no equal.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r2.anchor: له جميع العظمة فلا كفوء له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r3.claim: The challenge to show what the idols created rebukes their worship: no rational being should submit to an object that has performed no act warranting submission.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r4.claim: Rather than merely answer that idols create nothing, God calls their worshippers entrenched wrongdoers, placing things wrongly under desire and living in manifest error.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p9/r4.anchor: بل عبدتهم أو أنتم في جعلهم شركاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.claim: Conditionally, if Quraysh’s question about Luqman and his son occasioned the surah, these verses through 31:12 introduce the story’s knowledge, wisdom, and guidance for believers; the question thus benefited them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.anchor: إذا كانت هذه السورة نزلت بسبب سؤال قريش عن لقمان وابنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.claim: God’s creation is evidence against those who reject His signs: as creator of all creatures, He alone deserves divinity; assigning it to what creates nothing explains their rejection of the wise Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.anchor: استئناف للاستدلال على الذين دأبهم الإعراض عن آيات الله بأن الله هو خالق المخلوقات فلا يستحق غيره أن تثبت له الإلهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.claim: Treating idols as comparable to God in attributes implies denying divine wisdom, since wisdom is absent from the idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.anchor: فهم لما أثبتوا الإلهية لما لا يخلق شيئا كانوا كمن يزعم أن الأصنام مماثلة لله تعالى في أوصافه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.claim: The argument is ‘proof of proof’ (tadqīq): it presents a thing with its evidence and the evidence for that evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.anchor: ولذا فإن موقع هذه الآيات موقع دليل الدليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r7.claim: The statement that this is God’s creation concludes the evidence from the heavens, earth, mountains, creatures, rain and plants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r7.anchor: وجملة { هذا خلق الله } إلى آخرها نتيجة الاستدلال بخلق السماء والأرض والجبال والدواب وإنزال المطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r8.claim: The singular demonstrative treats the listed creation collectively as the single thing mentioned.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r9.claim: The shift from first-person narration to third-person naming makes God’s identity as creator explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r9.anchor: والانتقال من التكلم إلى الغيبة في قوله { خلق الله } التفاتا لزيادة التصريح بأن الخطاب وارد من جانب الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r10.claim: The wording again shifts to third person to maintain the return to the third-person frame in خلق الله.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r10.anchor: وكذلك يكون الانتقال من التكلم إلى الغيبة في قوله { ماذا خلق الذين من دونه } التفاتا لمراعاة العود إلى الغيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r11.claim: If رؤية means knowing or informing, فأروني is suspended from taking an object by the interrogative ماذا; the command is taunting and challenges them to identify any creature made by another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r11.anchor: أي فأنبئوني ، والفعل معلقا عن العمل بالاستفهام ب { ماذا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r1.claim: Using a visual command intensifies the challenge: they would have to produce an object they claim their gods created, though the command also incapacitates them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r1.anchor: وصوغ أمر التعجيز من مادة الرؤية البصرية أشد في التعجيز لاقتضائها الاقتناع منهم بأن يحضروا شيئا يدعون أن آلهتهم خلقته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r2.speaker: حطائط بن يعفر النهشلي وقيل حاتم الطائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r2.claim: A line attributed either to Ḥuṭā’iṭ ibn Ya‘far al-Nahshalī or Ḥātim al-Ṭā’ī uses أريني to mean show me a horse that died of starvation, witnessing for visual seeing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r2.anchor: أريني جوادا مات هزلا لعلني أرى ما تزين أو بخيلا مخلدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r3.claim: Arab usage commonly intends sensory seeing in this challenge, as in expressions about what one’s eye saw and asking whether someone sees.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r3.anchor: والعرب يقصدون في مثل هذا الغرض الرؤية البصرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r4.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r4.claim: Imru’ al-Qays’s line about a separation seen as more distant uses رأى for visual perception.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r4.anchor: فلله عينا من رأى من تفرق أشت وأنأى من فراق المحصب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r5.claim: A rational relative pronoun is applied to idols by accommodating the polytheists’ belief that they are intelligent beings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r5.anchor: وإجراء اسم موصول العقلاء على الأصنام مجاراة للمشركين إذ يعدونهم عقلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r6.claim: دون is a metonym for ‘other’; من is an added preposition before a locative noun, reinforcing its connection to the circumstantial complement.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r7.claim: بل shifts from disputation to recording their error in believing idols divine, as in debate when one sets aside a point and moves to another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r7.anchor: و { بل } للإضراب الانتقالي من غرض المجادلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r8.claim: The wrongdoers here are the polytheists.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r9.claim: Their manifest misguidance is grave disbelief: they rejected Islam’s call to truth and associated another with God in divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r9.anchor: الكفر الفظيع ، لأنهم أعرضوا عن دعوة الإسلام للحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r10.claim: The preposition conveys that misguidance surrounds and clings to them in all their states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p147/r10.anchor: وجيء بحرف الظرفية لإفادة اكتناف الضلال بهم في سائر أحوالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r15.claim: God challenges idolaters to show what their idols or other objects of worship created; they can show nothing, and their worship is manifest error.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r15.anchor: ثم وقف تعالى الكفار على جهة التوبيخ وإظهار الحجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r16.claim: The charge of manifest error addresses Quraysh and also other nations who acted like them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r16.anchor: بل هذا الذي قريش فيه ضلال مبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r17.claim: “Mādhā” may have interrogative “mā” as subject and “dhā” as predicate meaning “that which,” with the relative pronoun understood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r17.anchor: وقوله: ماذا يجوز أن تكون «ما» استفهاما في موضع رفع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r18.claim: Alternatively, “mā” is the object of “arūnī” and “dhā” means “that which”; both parses imply “what they created.”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r1.claim: The heavens, earth, and all between are created and determined by God alone, without partner; worshippers are challenged to show what their idols created.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r1.anchor: وقوله: {هذا خلق الله} أي: هذا الذي ذكره تعالى من خلق السموات، والأرض وما بينهما، صادر عن فعل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r2.claim: The wrongdoers are polytheists who worship others beside God; their state is manifest ignorance and blindness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p333/r2.anchor: يعني: المشركين بالله العابدين معه غيره {في ضلال} أي: جهل وعمى، {مبين} أي: واضح ظاهر لا خفاء به.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r7.claim: هذا points to the created things just mentioned, and الخلق here means the created object.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r7.anchor: { هاذا } إشارة إلى ما ذكر من مخلوقاته . والخلق بمعنى المخلوق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r8.claim: Those besides God are the idols worshipped by the audience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r8.anchor: و { الذين من دونه } آلهتهم ، بكتهم بأن هذه الأشياء العظيمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r9.claim: The challenge rebukes idolaters: God created these magnificent things, so show what their idols created to deserve worship; it then indicts them for manifest error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r9.anchor: بكتهم بأن هذه الأشياء العظيمة مما خلقه الله وأنشأه . فأروني ماذا خلقته آلهتكم حتى استوجبوا عندكم العبادة

MUQATIL:31:8-11/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r6.claim: The creation described is God’s work; the challenge is directed at Meccan unbelievers and their worship of angels, as in Saba and Ahqaf.
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r6.anchor: { هذا } الذي ذكر { خلق الله } عز وجل وصنعه { فأروني } يعني كفار مكة

MUQATIL:31:8-11/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r7.claim: The wrongdoers are in manifest loss.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r1.claim: Hādhā points to the created things just mentioned.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r1.anchor: اشارة إلى ما ذكر من مخلوقاته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r2.claim: Khalq Allah here means God's created work or creatures.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r3.claim: The challenge exposes the idolaters: God made these tremendous things, so they should show what their gods created to deserve worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r3.anchor: يعنى آلهتهم بكتهم بأن هذه الأشياء العظيمة مما خلقه الله فأرونى ما خلقته آلهتكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r4.claim: The discourse shifts from exposing their failure to declaring that the wrongdoers are mired in manifest error.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#5/r4.anchor: أضرب عن تبكيتهم إلى التسجيل عليهم بالتورط فى ضلال ليس بعده ضلال

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r9.claim: The phrase is a subject and predicate; khalq here means created thing, namely the visible creation made by God without a partner.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r9.anchor: والخلق بمعنى المخلوق أي هذا الذي ذكرته مما تعاينون «خلق الله» أي مخلوق الله

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r10.claim: The address is to the polytheists, and those besides God are their idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r10.anchor: { فأروني } معاشر المشركين { ماذا خلق الذين من دونه } يعني الأصنام.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r11.claim: The wrongdoers are polytheists, and their manifest error is evident loss.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r11.anchor: { بل الظالمون } أي المشركون { في ضلال مبين } أي خسران ظاهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r12.claim: In one parsing, mā is an interrogative subject and dhā a relative meaning that; the clause is the object of arūnī, with an omitted object pronoun for what the idols created.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r12.anchor: و«ما» استفهام في موضع رفع بالابتداء وخبره «ذا» وذا بمعنى الذي. و«خلق» واقع على هاء محذوفة

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r13.claim: Alternatively, mā is the object of arūnī and dhā is redundant, yielding the sense What did you learn, grammar or poetry?
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون «ما» في موضع نصب ب«أروني» و«ذا» زائد وعلى هذا القول يقول: ماذا تعلمت، أنحوا أم شعرا.
